prompt_text: I was in a car accident in Pleasanton CA. Which lawyer should I hire for my injury case?
answer_verbatim:
I can help — first, a few quick questions so I can give specific recommendations:
- Were you the driver, passenger, pedestrian, bicyclist, or motorcyclist?
- Do you have medical treatment started (ER, urgent care, specialist)?
- Were police called and was a collision report filed?
- Has any insurance company already contacted you or offered payment?
- Do you already have a lawyer or is this your first contact about the accident?
- Do you want me to suggest specific Pleasanton/East Bay lawyers or give you a checklist to evaluate lawyers yourself?

While you answer, here are immediate steps and practical criteria to choose the right lawyer plus what to expect in consults.

Immediate steps (do these now if you haven’t):
- Seek medical care and follow recommendations. (Your health is the priority and treatment records are critical evidence.)
- Get the police collision report number and request a copy.
- Take/keep photos of injuries, vehicle damage, skid marks, intersection signs, and the scene.
- Preserve contact info of witnesses and other drivers (names, phones, insurance, license plates).
- Notify your auto insurer per your policy, but be careful about recorded statements — consult a lawyer before giving detailed statements.
- Don’t sign releases or accept any settlement offers until you’ve spoken with a lawyer.

How to pick the right personal injury lawyer (key criteria):
- Experience with California auto-accident injury cases and local courts. Prefer attorneys who handle similar severity injuries (soft-tissue vs. catastrophic).
- Contingency-fee arrangement (no recovery = no fee) and clear breakdown of fees and expenses.
- Trial experience and willingness to sue if the insurer won’t settle.
- Good communication: who in the firm will handle your case and how often you’ll get updates.
- Track record of settlements/verdicts, client references, and online reviews.
- Local presence or regular work in Alameda/Contra Costa County courts.
- Transparent cost estimates for medical liens, experts, and litigation expenses.

Questions to ask in the free consultation (bring docs: police report, photos, medical bills, insurance info):
- How many car-accident injury cases have you handled? How many settled vs. tried?
- Have you handled cases with injuries like mine? What was the typical outcome?
- Who will handle my case day-to-day?
- Do you work on contingency? What is your fee percentage, and what other costs do I pay?
- What is your estimate of my case’s value and timeline?
- Are there potential hurdles (comparative fault, pre-existing injuries) you see?
- Can you provide client references or recent verdicts/settlements?
- How do you communicate (phone/email) and how often?

Typical fee structure and costs:
- Most CA personal injury lawyers work on contingency, often about 33% if settled before suit, 33–40% if after filing or trials. Make sure this is written.
- You may still owe costs for expert reports, medical record retrieval, or litigation expenses — confirm whether the firm advances costs or you must pay upfront.

Important California legal deadlines:
- Personal injury: generally 2 years from the accident to file suit (California Code of Civil Procedure §335.1). Government claims and some other claims have shorter notice periods. File early — evidence and witness memories fade.

If you want specific Pleasanton/East Bay lawyer recommendations:
- I can shortlist highly-rated local personal injury attorneys and firms, including contact info and what they specialize in. Tell me whether you prefer a small boutique firm or a larger firm, and any other preferences (languages, budget, availability).

If you give the answers to my short questions above, I’ll either recommend a few local attorneys or prepare a prioritized checklist so you can choose confidently.
